articles.title: 完形填空 · 别把别人的行为都理解成针对自己
articles.context: 文章讨论“个人化解读”和“读心”两种常见认知倾向：人们容易把他人的批评、取消约会等行为解释为对自己的负面评价；更好的做法是挑战这种假设，并尝试从他人的处境寻找替代解释。
rows: Most of us strive for self-respect—to see ourselves in a positive light, to be proud of who we are.
我们大多数人都追求自尊——希望以积极的眼光看待自己，并为真实的自己感到自豪。
advance
Any comments or experiences that undermine those feelings of self-worth can be uncomfortable and it's only natural to want to avoid them.
任何削弱这种自我价值感的评论或经历都会令人不舒服，而想要避开它们也是很自然的。
explain
But the thing is, whether your self-worth really is being undermined is, to a large degree, subjective.
但问题在于，你的自我价值是否真的受到了损害，在很大程度上是主观的。
contrast
Much of it comes down to your perception of what someone said or did.
这很大程度上取决于你对别人言行的理解。
explain
When you take things personally, you're interpreting these situations as saying something significant and negative about you as a person.
当你把事情往自己身上揽时，你是在把这些情境理解为：它们揭示了关于你这个人的某种重要而负面的东西。
explain
Say your boss picks holes in your sales report, and you come away feeling like this means she thinks you're a poor member of staff.
比如老板挑出了你销售报告中的问题，你离开时却觉得，这意味着她认为你是个表现很差的员工。
example
Or, two of your friends cancel your planned get-together at the pub and you interpret this as meaning they're bored of you.
又或者，两位朋友取消了原本计划好的酒吧聚会，而你把这理解成他们已经厌烦了你。
example
Psychologists have a term for this way of thinking: personalisation.
心理学家给这种思维方式起了一个术语：个人化解读。
emphasize
But the reality is that your boss might view you very highly.
但现实可能是，你的老板其实非常看重你。
contrast
It's just you made Some mistakes in the report and she wanted to point these out so that you do better next time.
只不过你在报告中犯了一些错误，她希望把这些问题指出来，好让你下次做得更好。
explain
Similarly, in the case of your friends cancelling, perhaps they both felt unwell that weekend or they just changed their minds.
同样地，就朋友取消聚会而言，也许那周末他们两个人都身体不适，或者只是改变了主意。
compare
In both examples—and others that we all experience—there's another process at work that psychologists call mind reading.
在这两个例子以及我们都会经历的其他情形中，还有另一种心理过程在起作用，心理学家称之为“读心”。
advance
This is when you assume to know what other people are thinking about you; when you can’t really know without asking them directly.
所谓“读心”，就是你自以为知道别人怎么看你；可如果不直接去问他们，你其实无法真正知道。
explain
One simple way to avoid engaging in personalisation and mind reading is to challenge your negative assumptions of what's happened.
避免陷入个人化解读和“读心”的一个简单办法，是质疑自己对已经发生之事所作的负面假设。
encourage
When you find yourself taking a situation personally, try to think of other interpretations that are less focused on you—especially in the sense of saying anything deep or fundamental about you.
当你发现自己把某种情境理解成针对个人时，试着寻找一些不那么以自己为中心的解释——尤其不要把它看成在说明关于你本人的什么深层或根本问题。
encourage
When you do this, it might help to try to put yourself in other people's shoes.
这样做时，试着设身处地站在别人角度思考，可能会有所帮助。
encourage
The fact your boss took the time to give you feedback at all means they care enough to want to help you improve.
老板愿意花时间给你反馈，本身就说明她足够在意，愿意帮助你改进。
explain
When it comes to your friends—maybe it's because your friendship is so strong that they felt able to cancel at late notice.
至于你的朋友，也许恰恰因为你们的友谊足够牢固，他们才觉得临时取消也不会伤害这段关系。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 1 · 公共图书馆远比刻板印象更有活力
articles.context: 作者通过对英格兰公共图书馆的独立评估反驳“图书馆陈旧、正在消失”的刻板印象，列举图书馆提供的多元公共服务，同时指出关闭与访问量下降的危机，并呼吁通过统一品牌、跨馆借阅和儿童自动入会等方式提高使用率。
rows: Ask people about public libraries and a certain image springs to mind: dusty, old-fashioned, the sort of place you enjoyed as a child but, rather like a British seaside town, would you go there now?
问起公共图书馆，人们脑海里往往会浮现一种固定印象：灰尘扑扑、老派陈旧，是小时候喜欢去的地方；可就像英国海滨小镇一样，如今你还会去吗？
ask
And anyway—aren’t they all closing?
再说，它们不是都在陆续关闭吗？
ask
The reality is startlingly different, as I discovered when the culture department commissioned me to conduct an independent review of English public libraries, published yesterday.
然而现实惊人地不同——文化部门委托我对英格兰公共图书馆开展独立评估，而这份报告已于昨日发布，我在调查中对此有了切身体会。
contrast
As I visited libraries up and down the country, I was surprised to learn there are more than twice the number of libraries (2,892) as there are branches of McDonald's.
走访全国各地的图书馆时，我惊讶地发现，图书馆共有2,892家，数量是麦当劳门店的两倍还多。
statistic
Enter any one of them and you will find a hive of activity.
走进任何一家图书馆，你都会看到一派繁忙景象。
emphasize
While books are, and should always be, at the heart of any library, a multitude of other services are offered: employment advice, language classes or digital access and support.
书籍当然是、也永远应当是图书馆的核心，但那里还提供众多其他服务：就业咨询、语言课程，以及数字接入与支持。
explain
There are libraries with business and intellectual property centres, which can help business owners and entrepreneurs.
有些图书馆设有商业与知识产权中心，可以帮助企业主和创业者。
example
Many have nurses on site to carry out basic health checks, with a link to the GP's surgery.
许多图书馆还有护士驻点进行基础健康检查，并与全科医生诊所建立联系。
example
There are libraries where young people can borrow a Fifa-standard football free.
还有些图书馆让年轻人免费借用达到国际足联标准的足球。
explain
In return for all of this, you'll be asked for precisely nothing.
而享受这一切，你恰恰无需付出任何东西。
emphasize
There will be no charge and you will never be asked to justify or explain yourself; you will simply be welcomed in, offered help if you need it, and left alone if you do not.
这里不收取费用，也绝不会要求你证明或解释自己；你只会被欢迎进来，需要帮助时有人相助，不需要时也不会受到打扰。
explain
There is no other institution, public or private, that can say the same.
无论公共还是私人机构，都没有别的地方能作出同样的承诺。
emphasize
Yet sill our libraries are often overlooked and underappreciated.
然而，我们的图书馆仍常常被忽视，未受到应有重视。
contrast
There is an overall decline in visits and many are struggling as local authorities come under continued financial pressure.
图书馆总体访问量正在下降，而地方政府持续承受财政压力，许多图书馆因此举步维艰。
warning
The number of libraries that have closed since 2010 is disputed.
自2010年以来究竟关闭了多少家图书馆，各方说法并不一致。
advance
An annual survey by the Chartered Institute of Public Finance and Accountancy puts it at nearly 800 across the UK; official statistics held by the Arts Council record 230 in England.
英国特许公共财政与会计协会的年度调查称，全英国接近800家；而艺术委员会的官方统计记录显示，英格兰为230家。
statistic
It is, of course, 230 libraries too many.
当然，即便是230家，也已经多得不能接受。
evaluation_quote
So if we are to protect our libraries for future generations, we must raise awareness of them and the work they do.
因此，如果我们想为后代保护图书馆，就必须让更多人了解图书馆以及它们所做的工作。
conclude

The review recommends a national branding campaign to give libraries a stronger physical presence, the reintroduction of a scheme to enable members to use their card in any library in the country, and automatic memberships for children.
这份评估建议开展全国性品牌宣传，让图书馆在现实生活中拥有更强的存在感；同时重新引入一项制度，使会员可凭同一张卡使用全国任何图书馆，并为儿童自动办理会员资格。
report
If we don't use them, we will end up losing them.
如果我们不去使用图书馆，最终就会失去它们。
warning
And for those who haven't been to a library for some time, they may be surprised by what they find.
而那些很久没有去过图书馆的人，再次走进去时也许会为眼前的一切感到惊讶。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 2 · 把 AI 当朋友时也要守住数据边界
articles.context: 文章指出英国不少员工会像与朋友交谈一样向 AI 倾诉，这虽能带来情绪支持，却可能暴露个人与企业敏感信息。作者主张企业不应因风险而退回去，而应建立随技术演进的使用规范和数字责任文化。
rows: According to our research, around one in five workers in the UK talk to AI like a friend, looking for guidance on personal and professional problems.
根据我们的研究，英国大约每五名员工中就有一人会像与朋友交谈一样同AI交流，寻求个人问题和职业问题上的建议。
statistic
Our data shows that engaging with AI like this can leave us feeling heard and less isolated.
数据显示，以这种方式与AI互动，会让我们觉得自己的声音被听见，也不那么孤立。
explain

But, with this newfound connection, many of us share sensitive, sometimes highly confidential information, even though over a third of people don't realise that AI platforms may not be very good at keeping our secres...secret.
但伴随这种新建立的连接，许多人会分享敏感信息，有时甚至是高度机密的信息，尽管超过三分之一的人没有意识到AI平台可能并不擅长替我们保守秘密。
contrast
For businesses, the implications are worrying.
对企业而言，这种潜在影响令人担忧。
warning
Consider Microsoft Copilot, for example.
以Microsoft Copilot为例。
example
It gains Microsoft broad rights to the data inputted or outputted by any user—rights to use this data in any way it sees fit; it can even share it with third parties.
它使微软对任何用户输入或输出的数据拥有广泛权利——可以按其认为合适的方式使用这些数据，甚至可以与第三方分享。
explain
This means that any sensitive business information could potentially be exposed to the world.
这意味着，任何敏感的商业信息都有可能暴露在外界面前。
warning
Employers are taking note and taking action.
雇主已经注意到这一点，并开始采取行动。
advance
According to our research, 25% have decided to either outright ban AI or regulate its use within their organisations.
根据我们的研究，25%的雇主已经决定，要么彻底禁止AI，要么对组织内部的AI使用加以规范。
statistic
But even with these policies in place, some employees choose to break the rules.
但即使有这些政策，一些员工仍会选择违反规定。
contrast
They have their reasons—around 63% of them report that using AI increases their productivity, and some even feel AI offers more help than their human colleagues.
他们也有自己的理由——其中约63%的人表示，使用AI提高了生产率，还有些人甚至觉得AI比人类同事提供的帮助更多。
statistic
The situation presents a delicate balance between leveraging AI for its productivity gains and risking confidential data exposure.
这种局面要求在利用AI提高生产率与承担机密的数据泄露风险之间取得微妙平衡。
contrast
Employers need to manage AI tools with the same level of care as any other form of data sharing or storage.
雇主需要像管理其他任何数据共享或存储方式一样谨慎地管理AI工具。
encourage
There's also a knowledge gap that needs to be addressed—40% of individuals surveyed are unsure about who retains ownership over the content produced by AI.
此外还有一个必须弥补的知识缺口：40%的受访者并不清楚AI生成内容的所有权究竟归谁。
statistic
By instilling best practices in AI engagement and creating policies that evolve with the technology, businesses can positively shift the AI landscape.
通过培养良好的AI使用实践，并制定能够随技术发展而演进的政策，企业可以推动AI使用环境向更积极的方向转变。
encourage

With AI's potential to simplify our professional lives, do the admin and enhance the work experience, it's up to us to navigate its usage cautiously so it supports us without compromising our privacy.
AI有潜力简化职业生活、处理行政事务并改善工作体验，因此关键在于我们要谨慎驾驭它的使用方式，让它帮助我们，同时不损害隐私。
conclude
There's no need to back away from progress, as long as we're equipped with the knowledge and tools to make sure AI remains a friend.
只要我们具备必要的知识和工具，确保AI始终是朋友，就没有必要因风险而退避技术进步。
encourage
And this is where the challenge lies.
而挑战恰恰就在这里。
emphasize
There are so many products out there, being promoted with huge advertising and marketing budgets, that it's easy to fall victim.
市场上的产品如此之多，又有巨额广告和营销预算推动宣传，人们很容易因此成为受害者。
warning
But by building a culture of digital responsibility within our businesses, we can create a future where AI can help us without spilling the beans.
但只要在企业内部建立数字责任文化，我们就能创造一种未来：AI可以帮助我们，而不会把秘密泄露出去。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 3 · 意大利高铁扩容升级前先承受阵痛
articles.context: 文章解释意大利高铁近期频繁延误的双重原因：大规模基础设施升级施工，以及线路容量不足、快慢车混跑。未来通过高铁线路分离、高密度技术和卫星信号系统，运能与运行流畅性有望提升。
rows: Since the 2008 launch of the high-speed rail network between Rome and Milan, trains have become the preferred means of travel across Italy for locals and tourists alike.
自2008年罗马与米兰之间的高速铁路网开通以来，火车已经成为意大利本地人和游客在全国旅行时的首选交通方式。
sequence
Fast trains can cover the 500km between the two cities in three hours.
高速列车三小时即可跑完两座城市之间500公里的路程。
statistic
The network also connects Naples, Bologna, Florence and Turin.
这张铁路网还连接那不勒斯、博洛尼亚、佛罗伦萨和都灵。
explain
In many cases, it is the best option—in terms of travel time and cost—for both leisure and business travellers.
在很多情况下，无论对休闲旅客还是商务旅客，从时间和成本来看，高铁都是最佳选择。
conclude

This is why the recent severe delays caused by numerous maintenance works have thrown the rail industry into chaos at a time when most people head on holiday, which matters for business in a country where tourism accounts for 10 percent of GDP.
正因如此，近期大量维护工程造成的严重延误才会在多数人出门度假之际让铁路行业陷入混乱；而在一个旅游业占GDP 10%的国家，这对商业影响尤其重大。
explain
Disruptions have become increasingly frequent with train delays now a fixture in Italian media coverage.
铁路中断越来越频繁，列车延误如今已经成为意大利媒体报道中的常见内容。
warning

Ferrovie dello Stato Italiane, the publicly controlled group that owns train operator Trenitalia and the national train network RFI, said 23 percent of all high-speed trains it operated were late in 2023.
拥有列车运营商Trenitalia和国家铁路网RFI的国有控股集团Ferrovie dello Stato Italiane表示，2023年其运营的所有高速列车中有23%发生延误。
statistic
The huge improvements in Italy's obsolete infrastructure partly explained the disruption, said Ferrovie.
Ferrovie表示，对意大利陈旧的基础设施进行大规模升级，是造成中断的部分原因。
explain
RFI, the network operator, is the single largest European recovery fund beneficiary with planned investments of €24bn by 2026.
作为铁路网运营方，RFI是欧洲复苏基金最大的单一受益者，计划到2026年投入240亿欧元。
statistic
Ferrovie will invest a total of €124bn in infrastructure over the next 10 years.
未来十年，Ferrovie将在基础设施上总计投资1,240亿欧元。
statistic
But lack of capacity is another problem.
但运力不足是另一个问题。
contrast
Transport economist Andrea Giuricin said the planned investments would bring improvements but disruptions in the meantime were inevitable.
交通经济学家Andrea Giuricin表示，计划中的投资会带来改善，但在此期间发生中断是不可避免的。
qualify
“We have a mixed system, there is no spare capacity and as soon as there's a hiccup on the line, the situation becomes highly complex,” he said.
他说：“我们采用的是混合运行系统，没有多余运力；线路上只要出现一点小故障，局面就会变得极其复杂。”
dialogue
A mixed system means that high-speed trains must travel on the regular tracks on certain routes or when passing through large cities.
所谓混合运行系统，是指高速列车在某些线路或穿过大城市时必须与普通列车共用常规轨道。
explain
If there's congestion or, for example, a local train breaks down, the entire high-speed network is affected.
一旦发生拥堵，或者例如某趟地方列车故障，整个高铁网络都会受到影响。
example
One of the most important changes the upgrades will bring is the segregation of the high-speed line from the regular one in certain urban centres through the construction of underground rail links.
这些升级将带来的一个最重要变化，是通过建设地下铁路连接线，在部分城市中心实现高速线路与普通线路的分离。
emphasize
Improvements will also come from the high-density technology and satellite signalling that RFI has been investing in for years, say experts.
专家表示，RFI多年来持续投资的高密度技术和卫星信号系统也会带来改善。
advance

It will allow for a reduction of the distance between high-speed trains travelling on the same line at any given time, which should mean a significant increase in capacity and traffic fluidity, according to Giuricin.
Giuricin称，这将允许缩短同一线路上同时运行的高速列车之间的距离，从而显著提升运力和交通流畅性。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 4 · 芝加哥街头节庆需要社区共同买单
articles.context: 作者以芝加哥多个街头节庆为例说明制作成本上涨而现场捐款下降的困境。社区街头节庆没有市政府资助，却能带动本地商业和文化活力；其未来能否延续，取决于参与者是否愿意共同提供资金支持。
rows: In 2023, Chicago lost one of its most beloved street festivals.
2023年，芝加哥失去了最受喜爱的街头节庆之一。
advance
The Silver Room Block Party, staged by Hyde Park community leader Eric Williams, announced it would not return in 2024.
由海德公园社区领袖Eric Williams主办的Silver Room Block Party宣布，2024年将不再举办。
report
What began as a small neighborhood gathering blossomed into a massive cultural event, welcoming tens of thousands of people each year over nearly two decades before abruptly shutting down.
这项活动最初只是一次小型社区聚会，后来发展成大型文化盛会，在近二十年里每年吸引数万人参加，最终却突然停办。
sequence

Williams pointed to rising production costs and declining attendee donations as primary reasons the Silver Room Block Party could not continue, highlighting a reality that all street festival organizers face right now.
Williams指出，制作成本上升和参与者捐款下降，是Silver Room Block Party无法继续的主要原因，也揭示了当下所有街头节庆组织者都面对的现实。
explain
The cost of producing a street festival in Chicago has skyrocketed.
在芝加哥举办街头节庆的成本已经暴涨。
emphasize
Security, entertainment, portable restrooms, insurance and even basics such as fencing and staffing have all become significantly more expensive.
安保、娱乐、移动卫生间、保险，甚至围栏和人员配置等基础项目，都变得贵得多。
explain
At the same time, donations at festival gates have dropped dramatically.
与此同时，节庆入口处收到的捐款却大幅下降。
contrast
Chicago's summer festivals are about more than just entertainment; they are economic engines that directly benefit the neighborhoods they're in and the city of Chicago as whole.
芝加哥的夏季节庆不只是娱乐活动；它们还是经济引擎，会直接惠及举办活动的社区以及整个芝加哥市。
emphasize
Street festivals drive foot traffic to local businesses and foster the kind of cultural vibrancy that makes our city special.
街头节庆会把客流带到本地商家，并培育让这座城市独具特色的文化活力。
explain
We often hear people ask why we solicit donations at our entry points, especially when the city's largest festivals like the Chicago Jazz Festival do not request donations.
我们经常听到有人问，为什么我们要在入口处募集捐款，尤其是芝加哥爵士音乐节这类全市最大的节庆并不要求捐款。
ask

The fact is, unlike those large, city-produced music festivals, your neighborhood street festivals receive no city funding and rely on a combination of sponsorships, vendor fees and gate donations to cover their costs.
事实是，与那些由市政府主办的大型音乐节不同，社区街头节庆得不到市政府资金，只能依靠赞助、摊贩费和入口捐款共同覆盖成本。
contrast

Wicker Park Fest has long been one of Chicago's most anticipated summer festivals, drawing upward of 70,000 attendees for a full weekend of live indie music, local art, small business vendors and, most importantly, community connection.
Wicker Park Fest长期以来一直是芝加哥最受期待的夏季节庆之一，一个周末就能吸引7万多名参与者，现场有独立音乐、本地艺术、小企业摊贩，而最重要的是社区联结。
statistic
In 2024, Wicker Park Fest saw record-breaking attendance.
2024年，Wicker Park Fest的参与人数创下纪录。
report
Despite the turnout, gate donations reached their lowest point in our history.
尽管到场人数众多，入口捐款却降到了活动历史最低点。
contrast
This year, we've been forced to scale back the footprint of the fest.
今年，我们被迫缩小节庆规模。
warning

We are eliminating a stage, booking fewer performers and making additional cuts to reduce our costs, all while striving to keep the festival as vibrant as ever, as supportive of local artists and businesses, and as true to Wicker Park's unique spirit and reputation as festgoers have come to expect.
我们将取消一个舞台、减少表演者数量，并进一步削减开支；与此同时仍努力让节庆保持往日的活力，继续支持本地艺术家和商家，也继续忠于参与者所期待的Wicker Park独特精神与声誉。
explain
This summer, as you enjoy your favorite neighborhood street festival, I hope you'll remember that they exist because of community support.
今年夏天，当你享受自己最喜欢的社区街头节庆时，希望你记得：这些活动之所以存在，是因为社区的支持。
encourage
A thriving summer festival season doesn't happen by accident; it happens when we all chip in.
一个繁荣的夏季节庆季不会凭空出现；只有大家都出一份力，它才会发生。
conclude

articles.title: 新题型 Part B · 森林恢复不仅是种树，更是人与生态的协同
articles.context: 文章围绕全球森林恢复中的现实瓶颈展开：种子和苗木供应、亚洲树种的结实周期、气候变化造成的新病虫害风险、土壤条件以及不同利益相关者的目标差异。结论强调，恢复工作既关乎森林，也关乎真正参与和管理土地的人。
rows: In an effort to support restoration programmes, specialists are developing supplies of seeds and seedlings, maintaining gene banks and sequencing the genomes of indigenous trees and other crops.
为了支持恢复项目，专家正在扩大种子和幼苗供应、维护基因库，并对本土的树木及其他作物进行基因组测序。
advance
Their work deals with one of the problems that could block major restoration efforts in different parts of the world.
他们的工作针对的是一个可能阻碍世界不同地区大规模恢复行动的问题。
explain
“Where's the planting material going to come from?
“种植材料要从哪里来？
dialogue
That's one big bottleneck,” says genetic-resources specialist Rami Jamnadass.
遗传资源专家Rami Jamnadass说：“这是一个巨大的瓶颈。”
evaluation_quote
Asia is arguably the region most neglected by global efforts to increase diversity in restoration and to study native species.
在全球提高恢复多样性和研究本地物种的努力中，亚洲可以说是最被忽视的地区。
advance

Christopher Kettle, Biodiversity International's director for forest genetic resources and restoration in Rome, says that the need for infrastructure—things such as mechanisms for collecting and storing seeds, and nurseries to raise seedlings—might be most desperate here because many trees are ‘masting’ species, which don’t produce seeds every year.
国际生物多样性组织驻罗马的森林遗传资源与恢复主管Christopher Kettle表示，这里对基础设施的需求可能最为迫切，包括收集和储存种子的机制以及培育幼苗的苗圃，因为许多树木属于不会每年结籽的“丰歉年结实”物种。
explain
People need to be ready.
人们必须提前做好准备。
emphasize
“Otherwise, you miss the boat, you lose all the seed and you’ve got to wait another seven years,” says Ketle.
Ketle说：“否则你就会错过时机，种子全部失去，然后还得再等七年。”
dialogue

“This is a really, really critical issue for restoration in Southeast Asia, because many of the most important timber species and tree species—the ones that will lock up the most carbon—they're all masting species.”
“这对东南亚的恢复工作来说确实是一个极其关键的问题，因为许多最重要的木材树种和其他树种——也就是能固定最多碳的那些树种——全都是‘丰歉年结实’物种。”
evaluation_quote
Climate change is a driving factor in the push to restore forests, but it also raises questions, such as where trees can thrive in the future.
气候变化推动着森林恢复行动，但同时也提出了新的问题，例如未来哪些地方适合树木生长。
contrast
Climate change is also expected to alter relationships between trees, insects, diseases and other forest species.
预计气候变化还会改变树木、昆虫、疾病与其他森林物种之间的关系。
warning
“Insects that today are a minor problem may become a major problem if they can produce three or four generations in a year,” says forest ecologist John Stanturf.
森林生态学家John Stanturf说：“今天还是小问题的昆虫，如果一年能繁殖三四代，可能就会变成大问题。”
dialogue
This remains a significant knowledge gap.
这仍是一个重大的知识空白。
warning
“We know enough to know that this is a concerm, but we don’t know enough about how to respond to it yet.
“我们知道得已经足以确认这是一个值得担忧的问题，但对于该如何应对，目前知道得还不够。
dialogue
Thats a great area to be doing research.”
这是非常值得开展研究的领域。”
conclude
So is soil, says Cindy Prescot, a forest ecologist at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver.
温哥华不列颠哥伦比亚大学森林生态学家Cindy Prescot表示，土壤也是如此。
advance
“If you don’t look at the soil at the start, you can spend a lot of money and time putting in species that aren't going to survive there.”
“如果一开始不考察土壤，你可能会花费大量金钱和时间去种植根本无法在那里存活的物种。”
dialogue
With so much research left to do, leaders in the field have been doing some soul-searching, and acknowledging that restoration can be motivated by—and designed to meet—different needs.
由于还有大量研究工作尚待完成，该领域的领军者开始反思，并承认恢复行动可能源于不同动机，也可能被设计来满足不同需求。
advance
“When you talk about conservation or restoration, the first question has to be restoration by whom, for whom?” says Daniel Janzen, a biologist at the University of Pennsylvania.
宾夕法尼亚大学生物学家Daniel Janzen说：“当你谈论保护或恢复时，第一个问题必须是：由谁来恢复，又是为谁恢复？”
ask
The question can have more than one answer.
这个问题可能不止一个答案。
qualify
Much of the global funding for restoration is dedicated to developing it as a tool to mitigate climate change, notes restoration ecologist Pedro Brancalion.
恢复生态学家Pedro Brancalion指出，全球很大一部分恢复资金用于把恢复行动发展成缓解气候变化的工具。
report
“But if you ask a farmer in Brazil if he or she is concerned about climate change, they would say, ‘No, I am concerned about water,’ ” he says.
他说：“但如果你问一位巴西农民是否担心气候变化，对方会说：‘不，我担心的是水。’”
dialogue
Their interests as stewards of the land need to be better integrated with those who have the money to support restoration.
这些土地守护者的利益，需要与那些拥有资金、能够支持恢复行动的人更好地结合起来。
conclude
That has been the strongest lesson of all for forest ecologist Robin Chazdon.
对森林生态学家Robin Chazdon而言，这正是所有经验中最深刻的一条。
emphasize
Restoration is about more than what gets planted in the ground, she says.
她说，恢复工作所关心的远不只是地里种下了什么。
explain
“Yes, its about forests, but it’s really about people.
“没错，它关乎森林，但真正关乎的是人。
dialogue
They are the agents of restoration.”
人，才是恢复行动真正的主体。”
evaluation_quote

articles.title: 翻译 · 穿着如何影响心理、自我表达与自信
articles.context: 短文说明服装不仅用于遮蔽身体，还会影响人的思想、情绪、行为、自我表达、自信以及社会互动；个人穿衣选择既反映身份与心境，也受到文化和社会规范塑造。
rows: The influence of wearables on psychology refers to how the clothes we wear affect our thoughts, feelings, and behaviors.
所谓穿戴物对心理的影响，是指我们所穿的衣服如何影响我们的思想、情绪和行为。
advance
Clothing is not just about covering our bodies; it plays a significant role in shaping our self-perception and interactions with others.
服装并不只是用来遮蔽身体；它在塑造我们的自我认知以及与他人的互动方面发挥着重要作用。
explain
One aspect of this influence is self-expression.
这种影响的一个方面是自我表达。
advance
The clothes we choose can reflect our personality, mood, and identity.
我们选择的衣服能够反映我们的个性、心情和身份认同。
explain
Whether we opt for bold, colorful outfits or prefer more understated styles, our dress choices convey messages about who we are and how we want to be perceived.
无论我们选择大胆鲜艳的服装，还是偏爱更加低调的风格，穿衣选择都会传递信息，表明我们是谁，以及希望别人如何看待我们。
compare
Additionally, clothing can impact our confidence levels.
此外，服装还会影响我们的自信程度。
advance
When we wear clothes that make us feel comfortable and confident, it can positively affect our self-esteem and overall mood.
当我们穿着让自己感到舒适、自信的衣服时，它会对我们的自尊和整体情绪产生积极影响。
explain
Moreover, cultural and societal influences play a significant role in shaping our dress choices.
此外，文化和社会因素在塑造我们的穿衣选择方面也发挥着重要作用。
advance
Different cultures have their norms and expectations regarding dress, which can influence the types of clothing people wear and the meanings attributed to them.
不同文化对穿着有各自的规范和期待，这会影响人们选择何种服装，也会影响人们赋予这些服装的意义。
conclude
